To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the four modes of communicative democracy identified by Young (greeting, rhetoric, narrative and argument) are useful for understanding how stakeholders interact in stakeholder workshops, (2) the four modes can be used to analyse video recordings of stakeholder workshops, and (3) the analysis of the video recordings suggests that stakeholder workshops are a rehearsal space for deliberation, where participants learn how to participate in inclusive ways.

(i) Young's modes of communicative democracy provide a robust framework to understand stakeholder workshop dynamics, (ii) stakeholder workshops are rehearsal spaces for inclusive participation that can be enhanced through improvisation and humour and (iii) the use of computer models can be a useful tool to facilitate stakeholder workshops.
1) stakeholder workshops can be sites for rehearsing inclusive participation, and 2) this is best achieved through improvisation and humour.

how workshops can be used to rehearse inclusive participation, and how this rehearsal can be more effective in real-world settings.
